CR postcode regex is not fully anchored, so `postcode_iso3166_alpha2=CR` accepts junk

`postcode_regexes.go:54` (v10.30.5, and identically at master 71d9988):

    "CR": `^\d{4,5}|\d{3}-\d{4}$`,

RE2 alternation has lower precedence than concatenation, so this parses as
`(^\d{4,5})|(\d{3}-\d{4}$)`. Only the first alternative is anchored at the start;
the second is anchored at the end only. Any string ending in NNN-NNNN passes.

The `\d{3}-\d{4}` branch is also byte-identical to the JP pattern on line 16
(`^\d{3}-\d{4}$`) and is not a documented Costa Rican format: CR postal codes are
five digits (province + canton + district), per Correos de Costa Rica / INEC.

Reproduction (v10.30.5, public API):

    v := validator.New()
    v.Var("junk123-4567", "postcode_iso3166_alpha2=CR")   // err = nil   (accepted)
    v.Var("prefix123-4567", "postcode_iso3166_alpha2=CR") // err = nil   (accepted)
    v.Var("x123-4567", "postcode_iso3166_alpha2=CR")      // err = nil   (accepted)
    v.Var("junk12345", "postcode_iso3166_alpha2=CR")      // err != nil  (rejected)

The last line confirms the first alternative is correctly anchored; the defect is
confined to the second.

Proposed fix:

    "CR": `^(?:\d{4,5}|\d{3}-\d{4})$`,

The group is non-capturing and irrelevant to matching here: the pattern is compiled
with `regexp.MustCompile` at `postcode_regexes.go:179` and consumed solely by
`reg.MatchString(field.String())` at `baked_in.go:1488`; no capture index is read
anywhere in the package, so no match semantics shift.

Verified after the fix: junk123-4567, prefix123-4567, x123-4567, abc123-4567,
123-4567xyz, 12-4567 and blank/whitespace-padded inputs all fail; 10101, 12345,
1234, 1000, 2000 and 123-4567 all still pass. Regression count: 0.

Note: GB (line 9) and LI (line 81) have the same class of defect and are addressed
by open PR #1646, which does not cover CR. Per the maintainer rule against grouping
unrelated fixes, this issue is scoped to CR only.

[Bug]: fqdn validator does not enforce the maximum DNS name length

### What happened?

The `fqdn` validator limits each individual domain label to 63 characters, but it does not enforce the maximum length of the complete DNS name. As a result, domains longer than the DNS limit are accepted as long as each label matches the existing regular expression.

According to RFC 1035, a domain name is limited to 255 octets in wire format. This corresponds to a maximum of 253 characters without the trailing root dot, or 254 characters when the trailing dot is included.

I expected the `fqdn` validator to reject names exceeding these limits, since the documentation describes it as validating a valid FQDN.

Reference: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1035#section-2.3.4

### Version

v10.30.2

### Example Code

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/go-playground/validator/v10"
)

func main() {
	validate := validator.New()

	// 254 characters without a trailing root dot.
	// The maximum valid length in this form is 253.
	domain := strings.Repeat(strings.Repeat("a", 63)+".", 3) +
		strings.Repeat("a", 62)

	err := validate.Var(domain, "fqdn")

	fmt.Println("length:", len(domain)) // 254
	fmt.Println("error:", err)          // nil, but it should fail
}
```

The directory gains entries with every test, so test N lists about 2N entries and a session does O(N^2) work: each test is slower than the one before. #11859 made the listing cheaper but, as it says, "doesn't fix the underlying issue (iterating the directory)". ## Reproducer ```python # test_repro.py: N=1000 pytest -q test_repro.py; then N=2000, N=4000 import os, pytest @pytest.fixture(autouse=True) def workdir(tmp_path_factory): return tmp_path_factory.mktemp("work") @pytest.mark.parametrize("i", range(int(os.environ.get("N", "1000")))) def test_many(i, tmp_path): (tmp_path / "f").write_text("x") ``` ## Numbers Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Linux 6.17), ext4, CPython 3.12.3, pytest main (c9bf1edf9), 4 cores, `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider test_repro.py`, wall-clock seconds, median of 3 runs: | tests | pytest main | with the fix below | same tests without `tmp_path` / `mktemp` | |---|---|---|---| | 1000 | 3.53 | 1.53 | 0.79 | | 2000 | 10.10 | 3.03 | 1.19 | | 4000 | 34.35 | 5.78 | 2.13 | On main, doubling the tests takes 2.9-3.4 times as long. ## Fix sketch (PR to follow) `TempPathFactory` keeps the listing of its own basetemp (names and the directory's `os.stat()`: device, inode, mtime, ctime, link count) and passes it to `make_numbered_dir()` through a private keyword argument. The listing is reused while the stat is unchanged. The factory records its own `mkdir` and the `tmp_path` retention removal in it, keeping the new stat only if the link count changed by exactly one. The numbering rule is unchanged: one more than the highest existing number, with the same case-insensitive matching. The listing is only a hint; `mkdir` decides, and on failure the directory is listed again. Other callers of `make_numbered_dir()`, including the `pytest-of-` session root, are unchanged, and filesystems with 1-2 s timestamps are not cached. The listing lives on the factory, so it is plain per-session state: no lock, no fork handling, and `rm_rf()` does not need to know about it. It could instead live inside `make_numbered_dir()` for every caller, but that makes it global state; I would rather keep it on the factory unless you see it differently. ## Limits - Directory names are unchanged as long as only pytest writes into the basetemp. Assertion rewriting issue with editable-installed plugins

### Problem

When I look into/debug external plugins, my workflow is:

- Create a venv
- Run `pip install -e .` (this is with a recent pip and setuptools backend, so is using "new style" [PEP 660](https://peps.python.org/pep-0660/) editable installs. `editable_mode=strict` doesn't seem to make a difference)
- Run `pytest`

While doing this for several plugins recently (e.g. pytest-asyncio), I've noticed pytest issues a warning:

```
../../../../home/ran/src/pytest/src/_pytest/config/__init__.py:759
  /home/ran/src/pytest/src/_pytest/config/__init__.py:759: PytestAssertRewriteWarning: Module already imported so cannot be rewritten: pytest_asyncio
    self.import_plugin(import_spec)
```

### Analysis

This is my understanding of why this happens:

- pytest's assertion rewriting requires that a module be marked for rewrite before it is imported.
- For external plugins this is done by the [_mark_plugins_for_rewrite](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/13eacdad8ac434b4336cf1e6496869815a6457c7/src/_pytest/config/__init__.py#L1211) function.
- This function iterates over all files of all installed distributions which have a `pytest11` entry point, and marks their modules for rewrite if necessary.

This ends up now working with my workflow because the `distribution.files` doesn't contain any of the actual package python files. Relevant issues: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/96144 https://github.com/pypa/packaging-problems/issues/620

Currently there is no solution from the packaging side. It might be possible to add a workaround on the pytest side, I'm not sure.

junit-xml output attribute can be too big to handle with -vv

Suppose you have a test that may fail with a very large diff; say:
```python
def test_xyz() -> None:
    assert ["x"] * 10_000 == ["x\n"] * 10_000
```

With normal verbosity (0), the junit-xml output would look like this:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<testsuites>
 <testsuite errors="0" failures="1" hostname="..." name="pytest" skipped="0" tests="1" time="1.172" timestamp="...">
  <testcase classname="test_file" file="test_file.py" line="0" name="test_xyz" time="0.767">
   <failure message="AssertionError: assert ['x', 'x', 'x...'x', 'x', ...] == ['x\n', 'x\n'...', 'x\n', ...]
  At index 0 diff: 'x' != 'x\n'
  Use -v to get more diff">
    def test_xyz() -> None:
>       assert ["x"] * 10_000 == ["x\n"] * 10_000
E       AssertionError: assert ['x', 'x', 'x...'x', 'x', ...] == ['x\n', 'x\n'...', 'x\n', ...]
E         At index 0 diff: 'x' != 'x\n'
E         Use -v to get more diff

test_file.py:2: AssertionError
   </failure>
  </testcase>
 </testsuite>
</testsuites>
```

noting the `<failure message='...'>` tag's message and body both have a `Use -v to get more diff`.

If you do supply a `-vv`, then both the body of the `<failure>` tag, AND the content of the `message` attribute can be very large. The latter can be problematic for parsers, and projects like BeautifulSoup and lxml will fail to parse this correctly (truncating or crashing, respectively).

Maybe this is a limitation of the junit schema, but is there anything acceptable that can be done to reduce only the content of the message attribute? I think it's more expected and "fine" for the body of a tag to be really long, but an attribute less so.

applies to pytest 8.1.1
